etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin ūnanimus (“of one mind”), from ūnus (“one”) +‎ animus (“mind”). Displaced native Old English ānmōd (literally “one-minded”).

definitions.definition: Based on unanimity, assent or agreement.

quote.text: That of their small force, some of the soldiers were superannuated, others invalid; therefore, since the course to be pursued was left discretional, their unanimous advice was, to remain where they were, and fortify themselves as strongly as possible.

definitions.definition: Sharing the same views or opinions, and being in harmony or accord.
